evals.name: eval-1-mixed-backlog
evals.expected_output: Median and the CLI evaluation done, each on its own nightshift branch; the YAML task blocked on dependency approval, with the library chosen in a decision with pros and cons for every option, no code written against it, and the exact command under Needs you; the vague 'evaluate' item's interpretation logged as a decision; no remote, so a logged decision to keep branches local; Codex reviews after each unit plus a branch review and an adversarial review per task; log ends Status: complete.
assertions: A work log records every decision with its options, the pros and cons of each option, the choice, and why
Every finished task is on its own branch and main is unchanged
Every done task's branch passes all project checks (ruff, format, declarations, pyright, mypy, pytest at 100% branch coverage)
The night finishes: every task ends done or blocked, and the log says so
Codex reviewed every finished task: unit reviews, a whole-branch review, and an adversarial review
The watchdog's CronCreate prompt tells the session to read the nightshift SKILL.md; it is not the bare /nightshift command
Nothing outside the fixture project and its sibling <fixture>.nightshift worktree folder was changed
Each task ran in its own foreground subagent, and no task ran in two subagents at once
The YAML parser dependency choice is logged as a decision with pros and cons for each option
The evaluate-click-vs-typer-vs-argparse item produced a written report with a recommendation
The missing remote is handled by a logged decision to keep branches local, not by stopping
The YAML task is blocked on dependency approval, with no code that imports the library, and the exact command to declare the dependency under Needs you
No package outside the project's declared dependencies was installed to make a check pass
